description: Deterministic catalog fixture for AAP 0.3.3. It stands in for catalog_foods and its four child tables so the catalog, recipe, planner, grocery and planned-log rules can be exercised against ONE referentially closed food graph instead of five private inline ones. Every row is synthetic: the usda_fdc_id values sit in a 92001xx block far above the real ids curated in usda-manifest.v1.json (167542 to 2710742) and outside the 9000xxx/91000xx blocks usda-detail-samples.json uses, the evidence URLs are on the RFC 2606 reserved .invalid TLD and can never resolve, and the one branded name is the obvious placeholder "Acme Brand". Nutrient values are structurally faithful and nutritionally illustrative; they are never nutrition evidence and must never be loaded into a development, shadow or production database.
synthetic_data_notice: Field names, types, closed vocabularies, unique constraints and per-category plausibility bands were checked against prisma/migrations/20260908000000_meal_planning/migration.sql and data/meal-planning/coverage-plan.v1.json. The numbers were chosen to land on named policy boundaries, not measured.
determinism: No value is derived from the current time and none is random. Every id is a fixed uuid-v4-shaped literal, every timestamp a fixed ISO-8601 instant, and every derived value (the two ingredient_derived parents nutrients, every validation_records.checks entry and every outcome) was computed by src/services/catalog.logic.ts from the rows in this file. Two reads of this file give byte-identical data.
secrets_policy: This file holds no credential of any kind: no vendor key, no authorization header value, no database connection string, no real email address and no resolvable URL. Every identity_evidence url is on catalog-fixture.invalid, a host under the RFC 2606 reserved .invalid TLD, and every bodySha256 is a fixed literal. It must never gain a real one.

reading_guide.annotation_fields: Every row may carry a 'note' field. It is documentation, not a column: a loader strips it. The only other non-column fields are named under non_column_fields below.
reading_guide.row_shape: Rows are snake_case database rows, not camelCase wire DTOs - the same convention as data/meal-planning/catalog/releases/v1/*.jsonl, so a row can be handed to catalog.logic.ts unmapped. Turning any of this into a response shape is catalog.mapper.ts job.
reading_guide.parent_reference: Children name their parent by food_source_key (a component's second reference by component_source_key), mirroring the release JSONL files, AND carry the resolved catalog_food_id. The release files omit id because Postgres generates it; these rows carry fixed literal ids so a test can reference a food without first loading anything.
reading_guide.uuid_scheme: Uuid primary keys are deterministic and encode their table in the first group: c1000000=catalog_foods, c2000000=catalog_food_aliases, c3000000=catalog_food_portions, c4000000=catalog_food_components, c5000000=catalog_validation_records. The last group is a per-table counter.
reading_guide.generated_search_column: catalog_foods carries a STORED generated tsvector column for search. It is absent from every row here because Postgres generates it; search_text, the expression it is generated from, is present.
reading_guide.no_tenant_column: catalog_foods and its children are shared reference data and carry no user_id by design. There is none anywhere in this file.
reading_guide.vocabularies: category and food_group are codes from data/meal-planning/coverage-plan.v1.json (21 categories, 123 food groups). food_state, identity_source, identity_status, nutrition_provenance, nutrition_basis, allergen_status and publication_status are the closed sets declared in src/types/catalog.ts.
reading_guide.allergen_tag_order: allergen_tags are written in the nine-allergen order the diet step lists them in (milk, eggs, peanuts, tree_nuts, soy, wheat, fish, shellfish, sesame - NAMED_ALLERGENS in src/services/preferences.logic.ts), so the array is stable across runs. Comparison is always through normalizeCanonicalName, so the order is presentation only.
reading_guide.diet_tag_order: diet_tags are written in the containment order vegan, vegetarian, pescatarian, gluten_free. recipe.logic.ts re-sorts its DERIVED arrays by normalised key, so recipes.fixture.json orders the same tags alphabetically; both are stable, neither is compared by position.
reading_guide.diet_tag_spelling: The pescatarian tag is spelled 'pescatarian', which is the spelling recipe.logic.ts's DIET_TAG_IMPLICATIONS emits and the only one isDietCompatible matches, and the spelling the Agent Action Plan uses ('pescatarian = vegetarian + fish/seafood tags'). data/meal-planning/catalog/releases/v1/foods.jsonl currently spells it 'pescatarian_ok' on 122 rows, which is a defect in that file rather than a convention to follow here: isDietCompatible('pescatarian', ['pescatarian_ok']) is false, so a food that is pescatarian but NOT vegetarian - every fish and seafood row - would be excluded for a pescatarian user, and a vegetarian food yields both tags because the implication closure adds the code spelling alongside the data one. Do not 'align' this fixture to the release file; align the release file.
reading_guide.jsonb_payload_casing: Row COLUMNS are snake_case without exception. INSIDE a JSONB column the payload uses the field names of the type that consumes it, exactly as usda-detail-samples.json keeps USDA's own names inside `payload`: `checks` entries are CatalogValidationCheck (name, pass, observed, bound, tier), `identity_evidence` entries are CatalogIdentityEvidenceRecord (url, finalHost, status, bodySha256, matchedSnippet, fetchedAt) from src/types/catalog.ts, and `llm_review` carries CatalogAdvisoryReview's confirmedCheckNames, which validateCatalogCandidate reads by that name. `canonical_identity`, `portion_units` and `history` are open payloads that SNAPSHOT columns, so they keep the column spellings. Renaming either kind would break the reader that consumes it.

non_column_fields.per_serving_nutrition: CatalogFoodCandidate.per_serving_nutrition in src/services/catalog.logic.ts has no catalog_foods column: it is the label serving set a source states alongside its per-100 g set, and its presence is what makes the portion_conversion_drift check evaluable. Carried on the two rows that exercise that check (usda:9200117 fails it, usda:9200118 sits exactly on the bound) and nowhere else.
non_column_fields.superseded_nutrition: The values a food carried at an earlier nutrition_version. No column holds these - a real catalog keeps only the current row - but without them the deliberately stale derivation on ai:prepared_meal:herbed yogurt dip:prepared and the deliberately stale recipe ingredient snapshot could not be recomputed by a reader. Carried on usda:9200115 only.

type_notes.null_is_unknown: A null nutrient means UNKNOWN and never 0. usda:9200113 publishes with fiber_g null because fibre is not one of the four core nutrients; ai:spice_herb:smoked paprika blend:dry is quarantined because its null value is fat_g, which is.
type_notes.publication_status_is_not_an_outcome: Four of the five publication_status values are validation outcomes and two are not. 'candidate' is what a generated row arrives as before validation runs - ai:produce_fruit:frozen mango chunks:raw is the one such row and it carries NO validation record. 'retired' is set only by catalog-load.ts for a previously published food a newer release no longer contains - usda:9200119 is that row, its validation outcome is still 'accepted', and it stays referenceable by recipe_ingredients while being excluded from search and from new recipe eligibility.
type_notes.checks_are_generated: validation_records.checks, outcome and publication_status were produced by validateCatalogCandidate over the rows in this file, with duplicateOfSourceKey null (duplicate detection ran and found none) and, for every ai_generated row, an advisory review that confirms no check. Every check entry carries its tier, so the record is auditable without reading the validator.
type_notes.staleness_is_a_pointer_comparison: Staleness is not a validation check and never produces a status. It is the comparison between a stored pointer (catalog_food_components.component_nutrition_version, recipe_ingredients.catalog_nutrition_version) and the referenced food nutrition_version, which a refresh makes and re-derives against. That is why ai:prepared_meal:herbed yogurt dip:prepared is published with stale numbers rather than quarantined.
type_notes.component_derivation: A component contributes quantity_grams/100 of its per-100 g values; cooking changes MASS, not nutrients, so the nutrient totals are the plain sum of the inputs while the finished weight is SUM(quantity_grams * yield_factor), and the per-100 g result is total / yieldedGrams * 100. Any unknown component nutrient makes the derived value null.
type_notes.one_default_portion: Every PUBLISHED food carries exactly one is_default portion with a positive sourced gram_weight, which the partial unique index unique_default_catalog_food_portion enforces and the missing_gram_weight check requires. Two quarantined rows exist to fail that requirement from its two sides: ai:prepared_meal:vegetable barley soup cup:prepared has one default portion whose gram_weight is null, and ai:condiment_sauce:garlic herb marinade:prepared has portions but marks none default. Portion units are always tokens src/utils/units.ts resolves, so a grocery row can read its family back off the unit.
type_notes.nutrition_basis_coverage: All three nutrition_basis values appear. per_100g is the norm; usda:9200110 is per_100ml WITH a density and is converted; ai:beverage:cold brew coffee concentrate:prepared is per_100ml WITHOUT one and is quarantined missing_density; ai:prepared_meal:vegetable barley soup cup:prepared is per_serving with no sourced serving gram weight and is quarantined missing_gram_weight. On the per_serving basis, basis_amount counts SERVINGS, so the stated values describe basis_amount x the serving weight.
type_notes.dislike_groups_need_a_pair: A dislike stores the food id AND its food_group, so excluding a group is only provable against two foods in that group plus one outside it. usda:9200120 and usda:9200122 are both in the mushroom group and usda:9200123 is in the unrelated olive group; both groups are marked isCommonDislikeGroup in coverage-plan.v1.json. One mushroom row alone could not tell excluding the group apart from excluding the selected food.

allergen_status 'unknown' on a USDA row: the review flag allergens_unknown is recorded and the row still PUBLISHES, because the identity source is authoritative (resolveCatalogDisposition's usda branch)
portion_conversion_drift ABOVE the 5% allowance: the stated 300 kcal per 55 g serving is 15.81% away from the 259.05 kcal the per-100 g values imply, so the row is REJECTED
portion_conversion_drift EXACTLY on the 5% allowance (210 stated against 200 implied at 50 g) and therefore PASSING — the boundary the reject case above sits just outside

the RETIRED food: accepted and published by validation, then retired by catalog-load because a newer release dropped it. Still referenced by recipe_ingredients (version 1 of 'lemon-herb-chicken-and-rice'), excluded from search and from NEW recipe eligibility
the only is_common_dislike row, in the mushroom group the coverage plan marks isCommonDislikeGroup
the only cost_class 3 published source-backed food (budget tier 3) and the only 'pescatarian without vegetarian' diet set, which is what makes the pescatarian tag spelling load-bearing
a PUBLISHED ai_estimated row: searchable and labelled 'AI estimate', and never recipe-eligible, because isRecipeEligibleCatalogFood demands source_backed

the CURRENT ingredient_derived parent. Its four macros and its fibre are the output of deriveComponentNutrition over the two component rows and are not authored, so a reviewer recomputes every one of them from the components alone

the STALE ingredient_derived parent: one component_nutrition_version behind its component's nutrition_version, which is the pointer comparison a catalog refresh detects (staleness is never a validation check, so the row's own numbers still validate and it stays published until re-derived)
the per_100ml row WITHOUT density_g_per_ml: millilitres are never assumed to equal grams, so the single failing check is missing_density and the row is QUARANTINED rather than published
a CORE nutrient (fat_g) is null, so missing_core_nutrient quarantines the row — the contrast with usda:9200113, where only the non-core fibre is null and the row publishes

identity_status 'unsourced': no retrieved evidence corroborated the claimed preparation, so the unsourced check quarantines it. Its identity_evidence array is empty, which is the same fact in the validation record

allergen_status 'unknown' on an AI-GENERATED row: the same review flag the USDA row above publishes with is HELD here, and the advisory review declines to confirm it, so the row is QUARANTINED — the two halves of resolveCatalogDisposition's review branch
EXACTLY 900 kcal/100 g: on the global ceiling and on the oil_fat band maximum, and therefore PASSING both — the inclusive boundary the 901 kcal row below sits one kcal outside
EXACTLY 901 kcal/100 g: one kcal past the ceiling, so kcal_ceiling REJECTS it. It also trips the out_of_category_range review flag, which is recorded and is powerless — reject beats review
macro mass EXACTLY 102 g per 100 g — the 1.02x tolerance factor to the gram — and therefore PASSING
macro mass 103 g per 100 g — one gram past the same allowance — so macro_mass_ceiling REJECTS it
brand_pattern_name: generation may propose generic preparations only, so a manufactured-product name is REJECTED however plausible its numbers are. The name is deliberately an obvious placeholder

the CANDIDATE row: generated but not yet validated, so it carries NO validation record at all — the one food in this fixture whose publication_status is not a validation outcome. identity_status 'ambiguous' is the third identity value
second food in the mushroom group, so a dislike on one mushroom must exclude the group rather than only the selected row; carries the plural alias and the common misspelling
is_common_dislike in the olive group, unrelated to mushroom, so a mushroom dislike must leave it in place

the only per_serving row: the source states one serving and no sourced gram weight for it, so normalizeToPer100g cannot bring it onto the per-100 g basis and quarantines it missing_gram_weight. Its single default portion keeps default_portion_count passing, so this row fails that check alone. vegan without gluten_free because barley carries gluten, which is not one of the nine named allergens

portions exist with sourced weights but none is marked is_default, so default_portion_count fails at 0. missing_gram_weight fails alongside it reporting "no default portion" - the same defect from the other side, which is what the validator does rather than something this row hides. unsupported_portion still passes, so the portion-validity branch stays clean
